newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW FIRST-HALF GROUP PROFIT SHARPLY HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: VW FIRST-HALF GROUP PROFIT SHARPLY HIGHER.

text.p: Volkswagen AG , the world's fourth-largest carmaker, said on Monday that group profit in the first half of 1997 surged 73 percent to 488 million marks ($268.6 million) despite a rise of only 12 percent rise in group global sales.

VW, the German carmaker which sells vehicles under the VW, Skoda, SEAT and Audi brands, said group net profit rose to 488 million marks from 282 million marks in the 1996 period. Group sales rose to 56.55 billion marks from 50.5 billion marks.

At the parent level, which reflects Volkswagen sales, VW said net profit rose 20 percent to 276 million marks from 230 million marks, while sales rose to 27.09 billion marks from 25.86 billion in the year-ago period.
VW noted that it was having troubles in the German market, saying sales during the period fell to 511,088 vehicles from 515,142 in the 1996 period.
One reason cited by analysts for the weaker German sales was that potential buyers were waiting for the launch of the new Golf model this fall at the Frankfurt car show.
Despite weak sales at home, VW said its global vehicle sales rose nine percent to 2.185 million units from 2.015 million in the 1996 period.
Production in the VW group rose to 2.207 million vehicles, up eight percent from 2.040 million, while vehicle deliveries rose 10 percent to 2.194 million units from 1.996 million.
